the loading door nobody watches
whoever is standing in it at two in the morning

quests.title: The Window Above Tempe
quests.blurb: The council knows and the council does not care. 5 years above Tempe. This is the third time I have had this conversation. I do not hear the trains any more, which means I hear it instantly when one of them is wrong. Since every second Friday the joins sound different. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

steps.label: ride it and listen to the joins
photograph the stretch that sounds wrong
tell me I am not mad

the bloke with the extra trestle

quests.title: The Clock at Victoria Cross
quests.blurb: Two people have already said no. The clock on the Victoria Cross platform has been four minutes fast since I got here and every relief who comes through wants to fix it. There is a version of this where I am the unreasonable one. Do not fix it. Find out who set it that way, before they retire. Be polite about it. It costs nothing.

steps.label: the clock, four minutes fast, for the file
to North Sydney, where the old crew drink
bring the name back

quests.title: The Dog at Concord West
quests.blurb: Do not laugh. A dog meets the 5:40 at Concord West every weekday and nobody gets off for it. There is probably a simple explanation and I would love to hear it. Four months of this. I have decided it is not going to be a sad story. Find out whose it is. I would rather know than wonder.

steps.label: the end of the platform, at twenty to six
the collar, if it has got one
the street it walks home to
tell me it is not a sad story

quests.title: The Book at Museum
quests.blurb: You are the first person to stop all morning. I run a small book on things that are not races — weather, delays, whether the two in the afternoon out of Museum runs on time. It has been going on longer than I have admitted to anyone. Somebody is beating it by information, not luck. Ride the run they ride. Come and find me after, either way.

steps.label: ride the run they ride
the two who follow you off it
$51 back off the book

Ride it to Randwick, photograph the platform with nobody on it, and come back and tell me the place still exists when there is no one in it. Whatever you find, bring it to me first.

the empty platform, lit and pointless
tell them what you saw

apply the shame manually
